title: Character Frequency
directAnswer: Iterate the characters, doing `freq[ch] = freq.getOrDefault(ch, 0) + 1`. The map is the frequency table.

remember.takeaway: The character frequency map underlies most string-counting problems.

problemStatement: Given a string `s`, return a map from each character to how many times it appears.
understanding: A hash map keyed by character, incremented per occurrence.

approaches.name: Hash map counting
approaches.whenToMention: This is the standard, expected solution — lead with it.
approaches.explanation:
Build a hash map from character to count in one pass — the string twin of the array frequency map, and the seed for anagrams, first-unique-character, and many string problems.

**Why getOrDefault / Counter.** On a character's first appearance there's no entry yet; `getOrDefault(ch, 0)` (Java) or `collections.Counter` (Python) supplies the implicit 0 so you don't NullPointer / KeyError.

**Case sensitivity.** Decide up front whether 'A' and 'a' are the same key. Lower-casing first merges them; keeping them distinct is also valid — just be explicit so it matches the spec.

**Array alternative.** For a known small alphabet (a–z), an `int[26]` is faster and O(1) space versus a hash map — worth mentioning.
hints: Map each character to a running count.
Use a default of 0 for first sightings.
approaches.complexityReasoning: one O(1) map update per character; the map holds k ≤ alphabet-size keys.

edgeCases.behavior: Two keys if case-sensitive, one if folded.

pitfalls: No default for a first occurrence (NullPointerException in Java).
Mismatching the case-sensitivity the prompt expects.

commonMistakes: Lower-casing when the prompt is case-sensitive (or vice versa).

followupVariations.title: First Non-Repeating Character
followupVariations.hint: Count, then re-scan for the first count-1 char.

patternNote: A core fresher pattern: Frequency map (chars). Master it on small inputs and it transfers to harder problems.
